pomo-01-c3.text: Peter Gratton (2018). Jean-François Lyotard. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
pomo-01-c3.quote: I define postmodern as incredulity toward metanarratives.
pomo-01-c3.claim: The second is incredulity toward metanarratives, Lyotard's signature line.

pomo-09-c1.text: Baghramian, Maria, Carter, J. Adam (2015). Relativism. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
pomo-09-c1.quote: Plato’s attempted refutation of Protagoras, known as peritrope or “turning around”, is the first of the many attempts to show that relativism is self-refuting.
pomo-09-c1.claim: The oldest objection to relativism, traceable to Plato's Theaetetus against Protagoras, is that it refutes itself.

pomo-02-c1.text: Gratton, Peter (2018). Jean François Lyotard. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
pomo-02-c1.quote: I define postmodern as incredulity toward metanarratives.
pomo-02-c1.claim: "I define postmodern as incredulity toward metanarratives" (incrédulité à l'égard des métarécits).

pomo-02-c1.text: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Lyotard, Jean-François. Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
pomo-02-c1.quote: In modernity the narrative of science was legitimated by one of a number of metanarratives, the two principal ones being respectively Hegelian and Marxist in nature.
pomo-02-c1.claim: Modernity ran on two principal ones, Lyotard argues:

pomo-03-c1.text: Aylesworth, Gary (2005). Postmodernism. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
pomo-03-c1.quote: Baudrillard argues that all of these realities have become simulations, that is, signs without any referent
pomo-03-c1.claim: Signs circulate without referents; the question "what is this image of?" becomes increasingly difficult to answer.

pomo-08-c1.text: EBSCO Research Starters. Physicist Publishes a Deliberately Fraudulent Article. EBSCO Research Starters.
pomo-08-c1.quote: Journal editors published Sokal's essay in the Spring/Summer, 1996, 'Science Wars' issue of Social Text.
pomo-08-c1.claim: In spring 1996, the cultural-studies journal Social Text published "Transgressing the Boundaries: Toward a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity," by Alan Sokal, a physicist at NYU.

pomo-06-c1.text: Catherine Slessor (2022). Pruitt-Igoe's demolition (modernism's death greatly exaggerated). Dezeen.
pomo-06-c1.quote: Modern architecture died in St Louis Missouri on July 15, 1972 at 3.32pm (or thereabouts)
pomo-06-c1.claim: Charles Jencks famously dated the death of architectural modernism to 15 July 1972, 3:32 p.m., the demolition of the Pruitt–Igoe housing project.

pomo-10-c2.text: Timotheus Vermeulen and Robin van den Akker (2010). Notes on Metamodernism. Journal of Aesthetics & Culture.
pomo-10-c2.quote: the oscillation between a typically modern commitment and a markedly postmodern detachment.
pomo-10-c2.claim: The most-cited candidate name for the successor sensibility is metamodernism, articulated by Timotheus Vermeulen and Robin van den Akker in their 2010 Journal of Aesthetics & Culture essay "Notes on Metamodernism."

pomo-04-c1.text: Fredric Jameson (1984). Postmodernism, or The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism. New Left Review I/146.
